network.name: Downtown Manhattan · East Village grid
network.disclaimer: Simplified Manhattan (East Village) network · geometry from Google Maps · synthetic traffic
description: Simplified downtown Manhattan network (East Village), synthetic traffic, 24 signals. Drawn with avenues vertical ("Manhattan north"); the real grid is rotated about 29° east of true north.
Avenues west to east: 2nd Ave (one-way SOUTHBOUND, 3 lanes), 1st Ave (one-way NORTHBOUND, 3 lanes), Avenue A and Avenue B (two-way, 1 lane each way). Main arterials: 1st and 2nd Ave.

Streets north to south: E 14th St (two-way, 2 lanes each way, main crosstown), then one-way side streets E 13th (WB), E 12th (EB), E 11th (WB), E 10th (EB), E 9th (WB). Side streets and Avenues A/B are the minor approaches to protect from starvation.
Intersection IDs are <street>_<avenue>, e.g. S14_A1 = E 14th St & 1st Ave. Phase 0 = avenue movements, phase 1 = street movements.
notes: Intersection coordinates from Google Maps Routes API lookups (one per avenue × street), projected to metres, rotated so avenues are vertical, and snapped to the median position of each avenue and street.
Lane counts, one-way directions and turn permissions are approximate simulation assumptions; left turns from two-way approaches are omitted (no permissive lefts).
Every intersection is modeled as signalized with two phases (avenue / street). Pedestrians, parking, buses and bike lanes are not modeled.

selectionRule: Candidate must be a valid policy.
Screen: mean training score must beat the champion's training score.
Development score must improve on the champion by at least 1%.
Must win (lower score) on at least 50% of paired development scenarios.
Mean completion fraction may not drop by more than 0.5 percentage points.
Side-street (Allen/Pugh origin) P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
Overall P95 wait may not exceed champion × 1.1 + 2 s.
If several candidates pass in one round, the lowest development score becomes champion.
scoreDefinition: Primary score = total stopped vehicle-seconds (speed < 0.5 m/s inside the network, plus all time spent in external entry queues) ÷ total scheduled vehicles. Lower is better. Every controller gets the same 900 s demand horizon and 300 s drain; unfinished vehicles keep accumulating stopped time and are reported as residual backlog.

championHistory.label: Queue-responsive heuristic
championHistory.reason: Starting champion: stronger baseline on the development suite

candidates.name: coord-arterial-wave-1
candidates.hypothesis: Avenue platoons on 2nd Ave SB and 1st Ave NB stop at nearly every signal because the adaptive controllers run free-running cycles with no offset relationship; biasing the avenue phase with travel-time-aligned coordination windows will let platoons clear signal-to-signal, cutting the biggest avenue stopped-time blocks (S14_A2 1972, S13_A2 1420, S9_A1 1489, S10_A1 1378 s/episode) without touching any queue weights.
candidates.explanation: Keeps every intersection adaptive with identical minHold=12, maxGreen=[50,35], weights, phaseBias and hysteresis as the champion (queue weights untouched). Only change: coordination.enabled=true with the same 90 s cycle, adding 12 phase-0 (avenue) windows, each length 45 s, bonus 10. Offsets chase link travel times: 2nd Ave SB offsets S14_A2=0, S13_A2=8, S12_A2=15, S11_A2=22, S10_A2=29, S9_A2=36 (links ~7 s); 1st Ave NB offsets S9_A1=0, S10_A1=7, S11_A1=14, S12_A1=21, S13_A1=28, S14_A1=35 (links ~7 s). Bonus 10 is modest relative to queue/approaching terms so heavy side-street demand at the A/A B intersections still wins when needed; no windows on Avenue A/B or side streets, so cross-street protection is unchanged. Expected effect: fewer avenue stops and less blocked-by-downstream spillback into the avenue links, with side-street P95 and completion held.

candidates.name: coord-arterial-green-wave
candidates.hypothesis: The champion leaves coordination disabled, so adaptive controllers free-run and disperse platoons. Adding a 90 s coordination cycle with phase-0 windows offset by one link travel time along 2nd Ave SB (S14->S9) and 1st Ave NB (S9->S14) should let avenue platoons ride a green wave, cutting arterial stopped time and freeing green for cross streets.
candidates.explanation: Only the coordination block changes: enabled=true, cycle=90, and 12 phase-0 windows on the two main one-way arterials. Offsets follow measured link travel times: 2nd Ave SB S14_A2=0, S13_A2=8, S12_A2=15, S11_A2=22, S10_A2=29, S9_A2=36; 1st Ave NB S9_A1=45, S10_A1=52, S11_A1=59, S12_A1=66, S13_A1=73, S14_A1=81. Window length 40 s, bonus 7: strong enough to lock the avenue phase to the cycle grid (typical competing phase score is 5-9) but still overridable by a genuinely stacked side-street queue, so side streets/14th St are not locked out. All adaptive weights, maxGreens and fixed fallbacks are unchanged from the champion, so any delta is attributable to progression alone.

candidates.name: refine-AB-sidefair
candidates.hypothesis: At the twelve Avenues A/B crossings the side-street approaches (E 9th–E 14th) accumulate the largest stopped-vehicle times (e.g. 2652 s at S9_AA WB, 2332 s at S10_AB EB) because their single-lane, short-storage queues are under-weighted relative to the parallel Avenue A/B movements; raising the oldest-wait weight and biasing phase 1 at those intersections should serve them more often and cut spillback.
candidates.explanation: Targeted refine of the champion at the 12 A/B crossings (S14_AA/AB, S13_AA/AB, S12_AA/AB, S11_AA/AB, S10_AA/AB, S9_AA/AB): weights changed from {queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, downstream 0.8} to {queue 0.9, approaching 0.7, oldestWait 0.15, downstream 0.9} so long-waiting minor approaches compete with vehicle-count-heavy avenue queues and are less likely to be fed into a full receiving link; phaseBias [0,0] -> [0,2] favours the street phase; maxGreen [50,35] -> [45,45] gives the side street more green per cycle; minHold 12 -> 10 and hysteresis 3 -> 2.5 make the switch to a starving side street faster. The 12 avenue intersections (A1/A2) are left nearly as champion (oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.05, phaseBias [0,0] -> [0,0.5]) to protect mainline progression, and coordination stays disabled (Corridor Coordinator's lever).

candidates.name: spillback-starvation-guard
candidates.hypothesis: The champion over-weights approaching platoons (0.8) and under-weights oldest wait (0.04), starving side streets and allowing short Avenue A/B links to spill back. Replacing platoon anticipation with queue/oldest-wait priority plus maximal downstream protection, and rebalancing maxGreen toward starved side streets, should cut side-street P95 waits and spillback without sacrificing trip completion.
candidates.explanation: All intersections adaptive. Weights: queue 1.2 (from 1.0), approaching 0.2 (from 0.8), oldestWait 0.15-0.25 (from 0.04), downstream 1.0 (from 0.8). minHold 15 (from 12), hysteresis 5 (from 3). maxGreen: main arterials [45,35] (from [50,35]); E14 minor avenues [35,40]; other minor avenues [30,45] to favor starved side streets and prevent short-link spillback. phaseBias [0,0]. Coordination disabled.

candidates.name: refine-oldestwait-sidewalk
candidates.hypothesis: The champion's very low oldestWait weight (0.04) lets the loaded Avenue A/B phases hold green while minor side-street approaches accumulate long tails (E 9th WB 33 s mean, side-scenario P95 288 s). Rising the oldestWait weight and giving a small phase-1 (side-street) bias at the Avenue A/B signals, plus trimming the major-phase maxGreen, should cap those tails and reduce the side-scenario backlog, while a milder increase on the 1st/2nd Ave signals protects tails network-wide without conceding arterial throughput.
candidates.explanation: Changes vs champion (all adaptive, minHold 12, hysteresis 3, queue 1, approaching 0.8, downstream 0.8, coordination off, fixed blocks untouched): (1) 12 Avenue A/B intersections (S*_AA, S*_AB): oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.14, phaseBias [0,0] -> [0,1.5] (favours minor phase 1), maxGreen [50,35] -> [46,38] (bounds worst-case red for the 1-lane side streets, slight extra minor green). (2) 12 1st/2nd Ave intersections (S*_A1, S*_A2): oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.08 only. Expected: lower side-street P95/max and fewer side-street backlog episodes (side scenario), small or no change on arterial/balanced scenarios, no loss of completion.

candidates.name: wait-priority-side-bias
candidates.hypothesis: The champion's oldestWait weight (0.04) is too weak to prevent side-street starvation; increasing it 5× to 0.20 and adding a +2 bias to the street phase at Avenue A/B intersections will bound minor-approach waits, while keeping arterial maxGreen at 50 s preserves 1st/2nd Ave throughput so overall completion and P95 do not regress.
candidates.explanation: Changed weights (queue 1, approaching 0.5, oldestWait 0.20, downstream 0.9) at all intersections; maxGreen arterial [50,40], minor [42,45]; phaseBias [0,0] arterial, [0,2] minor; hysteresis 3; minHold 12; coordination disabled. Expected: lower side-street P95 and backlog, reduced stopped vehicle-seconds from minor approaches, no arterial capacity loss.

candidates.name: side-street-progression-band
candidates.hypothesis: The largest stopped-time blocks are on the one-way side streets crossing Avenues A/B (E 9th WB 2652 s at S9_AA, E 10th EB 2332 s at S10_AB, 2123 s at S10_AA) rather than on the arterials; these ~200 m single-lane links are served by free-running adaptive greens uncorrelated with platoon arrival. Low-bonus phase-1 coordination windows offset by one link travel time along E 10th EB and E 9th WB should cut repeated stops on those corridors without taking green from the avenues.
candidates.explanation: Only the coordination block differs from the champion; all 24 intersection blocks (mode, fixed, adaptive) are copied verbatim. coordination.enabled=true, cycle=90 s. Eight phase-1 windows with bonus 5 and length 35 s at the signals of the two worst side-street corridors, offsets spaced by link travel time along the direction of travel: E 10th EB S10_A2=0, S10_A1=26, S10_AA=50, S10_AB=75; E 9th WB S9_AB=0, S9_AA=25, S9_A1=50, S9_A2=75. The bonus is small relative to hysteresis 3 and typical queue scores, so it only tips near-ties: green shares stay roughly balanced and the effect is fewer starts/stops (2 s lost per green start) and less blocked-by-downstream spillback at the A/B crossings. Queue weights, minHold, maxGreen, phaseBias and hysteresis are unchanged.

candidates.name: ab-crosstown-maxgreen-rebalance
candidates.hypothesis: At the ten Avenue A/B intersections the crosstown one-way approach carries far more stopped-vehicle time than either avenue direction (e.g. E 9th WB 2652 s at S9_AA; E 10th EB 2332 s at S10_AB), yet the uniform plan caps that crosstown phase at maxGreen 35 s while the lighter single-lane avenue phase may hold 50 s; raising the crosstown cap lifts the binding constraint on the dominant movement.
candidates.explanation: Only adaptive maxGreen at the ten A/B intersections (S13_AA, S13_AB, S12_AA, S12_AB, S11_AA, S11_AB, S10_AA, S10_AB, S9_AA, S9_AB) changes from [50,35] to [45,50]: the avenue phase 0 keeps a 45 s ceiling (still far above its 6-8 veh storage), while the crosstown phase 1 gains a 50 s ceiling matching its 190-205 m / 25-27 veh links. All weights, minHold, hysteresis, phaseBias, the E 14th intersections, the 1st/2nd Ave intersections and coordination are unchanged from the champion. Expected: shorter crosstown queues and lower stopped veh-sec at the dominant bottlenecks without starving avenue movements or regressing overall/side-street P95.

candidates.name: ab-receiving-protect
candidates.hypothesis: Avenue A/B receiving links are only 6-8 veh (vs 18-24 on 1st/2nd Ave), so they spill back heavily (up to 121 s/ep) and block the worst side-street approaches (E 9th WB 2652 s, E 10th EB 2332/2123 s). Raising the downstream (receiving-link) weight at the twelve A/B signals suppresses an avenue phase only when its short receiving link is already full, freeing green for the cross streets and cutting gridlock, without touching any demand weights.
candidates.explanation: Single lever: adaptive.weights.downstream 0.8 -> 0.95 at the twelve Avenue A/B intersections (S14/S13/S12/S11/S10/S9 _AA and _AB). Rationale: their 6-8 veh storage fills fast (spillback 23-121 s/ep, blockedByDownstream up to 57 s) while their side-street receiving links are long (25-27 veh) and rarely suppress, so the change mainly stops dumping avenue platoons into full short links. All other parameters (minHold 12, maxGreen [50,35], queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, phaseBias [0,0], hysteresis 3) and all eight 1st/2nd Ave signals are unchanged, avoiding the starvation effects of the r1 weight/side-bias edits.

candidates.name: r2-queue-explore-capfair
candidates.hypothesis: At the twelve Avenue A/B intersections the green caps ([50,35]) systematically favour the avenue movement even though that movement's receiving links hold only 6-8 vehicles while the side-street approaches hold 25-27; the 35 s cap truncates service of the biggest single stopped-time blocks (E 10th EB / E 9th WB, 2123-2652 stopped veh-s/episode) while the avenue green overfills the short links (spillback 40-121 s/episode, blocked-by-downstream up to 57 s). Making those caps storage-symmetric so the queue score (not the cap) sets the split, and strengthening the receiving-link term, should drain
candidates.explanation: Changed parameters: (1) adaptive.weights.downstream 0.8 -> 0.95 at all 24 intersections, so a green that would discharge into a nearly full receiving link is almost fully discounted - targets the 40-121 s/episode spillback on the 6-8 veh Avenue A/B links (S9/S10/S11/S12_AA/AB, S14_AB). (2) maxGreen changed from [50,35] to [45,45] at the twelve Avenue A/B intersections (S14/S13/S12/S11/S10/S9 _AA and _AB): caps are now proportional to storage (side-street approach 25-27 veh, avenue receiving link 6-8 veh) and the 35 s truncation of heavily queued side-street phases is lifted; this is a cap change only, the score still decides the split. (3) All other levers unchanged (queue 1, approaching 0.8, oldestWait 0.04, minHold 12, hysteresis 3, phaseBias 0) and the 1st/2nd Ave arterial intersections keep the champion's [50,35] caps. Expected effects: lower stopped-time on E 9th WB / E 10th EB and less Avenue A/B link blockage, side-street P95 flat-to-better, arterial throughput preserved, coordination left disabled.

candidates.name: refine-AB-south-sidegreen
candidates.hypothesis: At the four worst side-street bottlenecks (S9_AA, S9_AB, S10_AA, S10_AB) the minor approaches wait 28-33 s mean while the parallel Avenue A/B movements are already spillback-limited by their short downstream links, so the avenue phase is holding green it cannot use. Rebalancing maxGreen toward the street phase and slightly raising oldest-wait sensitivity at only these four intersections should cut the largest side-street stopped-time blocks without touching arterial throughput elsewhere.
candidates.explanation: Changed only 4 of 24 intersections (S9_AA, S9_AB, S10_AA, S10_AB), which hold the largest side-street stopped-vehicle-seconds (2652/1722/2123/2332 s per episode) and also heavy avenue spillback (51-121 s): maxGreen [50,35] -> [42,42] (trim 8 s of avenue cap that is wasted behind full downstream links, give the starved street phase 7 s more green per cycle), and weights.oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.08 so a long-waiting minor approach can outscore a merely queued avenue phase. All other intersections, weights, hysteresis, minHold and coordination stay identical to the champion, so the well-performing arterial/balanced scenarios are untouched.

candidates.name: switch-cost-stabilizer
candidates.hypothesis: Every phase switch costs 5 s clearance plus ~2 s queue startup, and the champion's minHold=12/hysteresis=3 lets the controller oscillate every ~15 s, burning capacity and letting the short one-lane Avenue A/B links (6-8 veh storage) spill back and gridlock in the side/bursty scenarios. Holding each green much longer (minHold 20, hysteresis 6) and trimming the arterial over-bias (maxGreen 50/30 on 1st-2nd Ave, 42/40 at Avenue A/B) should cut lost time and clear long single-lane side-street queues (E 9th/10th WB/EB mean waits 28-33 s) in fewer cycles, without starving anyone because the 90 s for
candidates.explanation: Changed vs champion (all 24 intersections): minHold 12 -> 20; hysteresis 3 -> 6; weights approaching 0.8 -> 0.75, oldestWait 0.04 -> 0.06, downstream 0.8 -> 0.85. maxGreen: 1st/2nd Ave intersections (S*_A1, S*_A2) [50,35] -> [50,30]; Avenue A/B intersections (S*_AA, S*_AB) [50,35] -> [42,40] (removes the strong arterial bias that starves the side street at A/B crossings). phaseBias: +0.5 on the avenue phase at 1st/2nd Ave only. Coordination left disabled as in the champion. Expected effect: fewer clearance/startup losses, less oscillation under bursty demand, shorter side-street discharge tails and less Avenue A/B spillback/gridlock (side scenario completion 97.9%, backlog 44).
